coverage_analysis: The batch of source cases significantly involves criminal jurisprudence pertaining to sexual offences, age determination, and the evidentiary value of victim testimonies. The current LegalFlux template library contains templates on circumstantial evidence (LF004), medical vs. ocular conflicts (LF005), and interested witnesses (LF006), but lacks high-level reasoning models specifically designed for the unique evidentiary burdens in sexual assault cases. Analysis reveals recurring, unmapped operations: (1) convicting solely on the reliable testimony of a prosecutrix without requiring independent corroboration; (2) legally establishing rape based on partial penetration despite intact anatomical structures (hymen) or missing seminal fluids; (3) determining statutory age by strictly prioritizing primary documentary records (school/birth registers) over approximate medical/radiological tests; and (4) vitiating consent under Section 90 IPC when procured through a fraudulent, bad-faith promise of marriage from inception. These distinct reasoning patterns recur across multiple cases in the batch and represent vital gap candidates for the library.
